relevance_note: Case report of a PSTPIP1 p.E250K carrier plus a literature table of five further p.E250K carriers with kidney involvement: "revealing the heterozygous c.748G>A, p.E250K mutation".
method_note: Table 2 lists patients as columns under a 'Patient number' header row with bare numbers 1-6, so labels are 'Table 2 #1'..'Table 2 #6'; #6 is the 'Present case' described in the Case Presentation and Table 1, and all its text-derived facts are under 'Table 2 #6'. Column spans quote the row from its label through the patient's cell; where that exceeded ~300 characters (long 'Others', 'Kidney involvement' and treatment cells) the span is a list of the row label and the cell text. A Python script in the scratch directory built the JSON and asserted every span verbatim; Table 2 cells were read by the script and checked by eye against the table. Table 2 uses Y/N; the legend does not define N, so N cells were treated as not reported (no excluded rows). Table 1 uses +/- (not defined in the legend) per age column; '–' cells were not used as excluded, and 'Absent' proteinuria at ages 4-15 was not recorded as an excluded row because proteinuria was later present (temporal, mentioned here). Normal kidney function at 19 years ('with normal kidney function') preceded the later 'worsening of renal function'; only the later abnormality was recorded. 'familiarity for early gout' (#2) and 'familiarity for psoriatic arthritis' (#4) describe family history, not the patient, and were not recorded as features. Variant type 'missense' comes from the abstract sentence naming p.E250K. Zygosity is stated only for #6; others left not reported. MEFV p.E148Q 'carrier' for #2 recorded as a variant row with zygosity not reported. #1 age 35 is marked '*Age of death' -> deceased, P35Y; cause of death not stated. #6 source column reads 'Present case' and the patient is described first-hand, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'; the paper says he was 'previously included in a PAMI cohort (1)' (Holzinger 2015), recorded in publications. Possible inconsistency: the Discussion says 'in patient 4, colchicine was effective in reversing proteinuria', but in Table 2 colchicine (ND; complete) is listed for patient 5 (Dai et al.) and patient 4 received only infliximab; not recorded as a feature for either. Osteomyelitis in #4 is not stated as sterile (sepsis and cellulitis are also listed), so the checklist item 'sterile osteomyelitis or osteolytic bone lesions' was left not reported. Discussion counts (179 articles, seven reporting E250K/E257K, five with renal involvement) are group-level only.
